title: Get your gobble on: Thanksgiving crafts and games for all
text:
Get your gobble on: Thanksgiving crafts and games for all
Thanksgiving crafts and games that will keep your family busy while the turkey roasts.
Leaf art
Sometimes, the best crafts are the most simple. We’re also fans of activities that get you outside and looking at nature.
Materials needed:
Fallen leaves (look for relatively flat ones that have dried)
Need some time-gobbling activities before your big Thanksgiving meal? Then look no further. The Monitor staff has gathered some handmade fun for everyone.
White pen
Step by step:
This one is easy! Collect some fallen leaves – they can be any shape or size. If they aren’t
fully dry, you might want to dab them with a paper towel.
Next, use the white pen to make designs on the leaves. We like tracing the outside and following the veins, but use your imagination!
Let the painted leaves dry for a little bit. You can string them together with twine to make a leaf garland (either tie the twine around the stems or use paper clips) or scatter the leaves on your Thanksgiving table as decorations.
***
Becorns
Artist and toy designer David M. Bird began making and photographing these “little acorn people” in the late 2000s. In 2022, a Becorn video went viral on Instagram and the nature-based creations became his full-time work. You can check out his Becorns at art exhibits around the country and online – and you can also make one of your own.
Materials needed:
Acorns, pine cones, sticks, and other interesting
or delightful things you find outside 
Glue gun
Pens
Step by step:
Find an acorn or pine cone that you like the shape of; this will be your Becorn’s head.
Draw a face for your Becorn. Hot glue other acorns or sticks onto the head to create the body, arms, and legs.
See what poses you can create! Does your Becorn tell a story? Can you make it hold something?
***
Hand Turkey
The OG of Thanksgiving crafts, this one you can
pretty much make anywhere with materials you have (we can’t help it) on hand. 
Materials needed:
Paper
Markers, crayons, or colored pencils
Step by step:
Place your hand on a sheet of paper. Using a pencil or marker, trace around your hand and fingers.
Color your hand turkey. You might want your fingers to become different colored feathers; you might add a wing in the middle of your palm. On your thumb, draw your turkey’s eyes, beak, and wattle.
Add two legs, and you’re done!
